additional_concerns: The legacy exclusion in node.074087c89e3a3304960f612e, node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909 is an interpretation, not an express substantive disqualification. Preserving an application's existing process does not expressly establish a permanent bar to relief for the underlying change, including after a subsequent decision, withdrawal or resubmission.

Node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from scope rather than deciding their eligibility. Node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa decides substantive qualification only. Neither resolves actual relief for legacy applications; node.8eb374ffa546ddd2ba291e37 explicitly leaves that question without an executable rule.

The explicit commencement date supports a date threshold, but the source does not specify a universal assessment-event or implementation-date test. The introductory immediate-effect wording cannot independently be reconciled without publication-date evidence.

Additional authority needed to resolve actual transitional relief includes the relevant SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds FAQs and any SFC guidance on legacy applications, withdrawal and resubmission. Applicable home-jurisdiction rules are also needed to determine home compliance for a concrete change. These authorities are not supplied; the two unbound dependency IDs have no identified titles or mapping, so neither can safely be assigned.
Notification alignment and continuing post-vetting are separate from prior-approval relief. Their exclusion from these typed questions is not evidence that those obligations disappear.
